s.note: the salami his son takes and James makes him give back
s.how: Slice a baguette into 16 thin rounds, brush with olive oil and toast at 200C for 6 minutes until golden. Whip 200g ricotta with the zest of a lemon, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of olive oil until smooth. Spread on the toasts and top each with a folded slice of salami from 150g. Finish with a sliver of pickled onion, cracked black pepper and a few parsley leaves.

s.note: making a little go a long way
s.how: Heat 100g beef dripping in a heavy pan. Fry 8 thick slices white bread slowly until golden and crisp on both sides. Drain and sprinkle with flaky salt and cracked pepper. Serve hot.

m.note: Mae making one pot feed the whole family
m.how: Brown 800g diced beef shin. Add 2 onions, 3 carrots, 400g potatoes, 100g pearl barley and 1.2L stock with thyme. Simmer 3 hours until thick. Serve with bread to make it go further.

w.how: Tear 8 slices day-old bread into a buttered dish and scatter with 80g sultanas. Whisk 3 eggs, 500ml milk, 60g brown sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon and pour over. Soak 20 minutes and bake at 170C for 40 minutes.

d.note: the milk they can barely afford in the Depression
d.how: Pour 1L full cream milk into a saucepan with 3 tbsp honey, a cinnamon stick and half a tsp vanilla extract. Warm gently over low heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until steaming but not boiling. Remove the cinnamon stick. Whisk hard for 30 seconds until frothy, or use a milk frother. Pour into four mugs and grate fresh nutmeg over each.
